column1: # Vantage list for retail-vs-port parity captures.
# Format: name <TAB> level <TAB> x <TAB> y <TAB> z <TAB> pitch <TAB> yaw
# A "-" pose means: the level own spawn pose. Retail: load and read `coords`, no warp.
#                                Port: plain `--start <level>`, no `--shot-at`.
# Positions are the **camera eye** in game/world units; PYR are degrees in the retail `coords`
# convention. The retail side warps the player body to `z - 0.037` so the eye lands at `z`
# (`sithCamera_Update` rides `thing + 0x168`); the port warps its player the same way (the
# port-capture side passes `--warp "x,y,z,yaw"`, whose body also goes one eye offset below `z`) and
# keeps `--shot-at` to pin the camera to the recorded vantage. Both sides therefore have a body at
# the pose — scripts, AI and hazards react to it — not just a camera there.
# The `pitch` column is the **port camera** pitch in degrees. Retail's `warp` sets position and yaw
# only; its rendered camera pitch is not the `coords` PYR pitch (level 1 prints 1.04, yet a 0.25
# degree port pitch already drops the spawn pair 0.63 -> 0.59), so keep it 0 until a retail frame is
# measured to say otherwise.
# The route rows are the level's own `walkplayer` placements (things 167, 169, 170, 171 and 174 of
# 01narshadda) — the multiplayer start points — so every pose is an authored, standable camera in
# the cantina, on the way up, and at the upper door. Eye = thing position + the 0.037 eye offset.
# The staged JK.EXE is patched so `warp` exists (see Set-JkDevCommandsEnabled in retail-lib.ps1).
name
spawn
spawn_pose
spawn_yaw30
route_cantina
route_lower
route_street
route_catwalk
route_door

# -4.75,-3.75,-1.10) facing south, then press the use key. Phase 1 step 4's interaction probe.
switch_cantina

switch_cantina2
